nursing: Check the total paracetamol dose from all sources (combination products included) before giving. Do not exceed 4 g in 24 hours; monitor LFTs on prolonged use.

sec.Indications: Fever, headache, toothache, myalgia, backache and other mild to moderate pain; symptomatic relief of cold and flu.
sec.Dosage & Administration: Adults: 1–2 tablets every 4–6 hours as required, maximum 8 tablets (4 g) daily. Children 6–12 years: ½–1 tablet 3–4 times daily.
sec.Side Effects: Rare at therapeutic doses — skin rash and hypersensitivity reactions. Hepatic damage occurs in overdose.
sec.Contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to paracetamol; severe hepatic impairment.
sec.Drug Interactions: Prolonged regular use may enhance the effect of warfarin. Hepatotoxicity risk increases with chronic alcohol use and enzyme-inducing drugs.
sec.Pregnancy & Lactation: Considered safe in all trimesters and during breast feeding at recommended doses.
sec.Storage: Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light. Keep out of reach of children.

nursing: Controlled drug — record in the DD register. Monitor sedation level, respiratory rate and blood pressure; apply fall precautions. Watch for serotonin syndrome when combined with SSRIs.

sec.Indications: Moderate to severe acute and chronic pain, including post-operative pain.
sec.Dosage & Administration: Adults: 50–100 mg every 4–6 hours as needed; maximum 400 mg daily. Reduce dose in elderly, hepatic and renal impairment.
sec.Side Effects: Nausea, vomiting, dizziness, sweating, constipation, dry mouth, sedation. Seizures and dependence with prolonged or high-dose use.
sec.Contraindications: Acute intoxication with alcohol, hypnotics or opioids; patients on MAO inhibitors; uncontrolled epilepsy.
sec.Drug Interactions: SSRIs/SNRIs and triptans raise serotonin-syndrome risk; carbamazepine reduces effect; CNS depressants potentiate sedation.
sec.Pregnancy & Lactation: Not recommended — neonatal withdrawal reported; small amounts pass into breast milk.
sec.Storage: Store below 30°C, protected from light and moisture, in a locked controlled-drug cupboard.

nursing: Give at least 1 hour before a meal; tablet must be swallowed whole, not crushed or chewed. Review ongoing need — long-term use is linked to hypomagnesaemia and B12 deficiency.

sec.Indications: GERD, erosive oesophagitis, NSAID-associated gastric ulcer, H. pylori eradication (combination therapy), Zollinger–Ellison syndrome.
sec.Dosage & Administration: Adults: 20–40 mg once daily for 4–8 weeks depending on indication; maintenance 20 mg daily.
sec.Side Effects: Headache, abdominal pain, diarrhoea, flatulence, nausea; rarely rash and dizziness.
sec.Contraindications: Hypersensitivity to esomeprazole or other benzimidazole PPIs.
sec.Drug Interactions: May reduce activation of clopidogrel; alters absorption of ketoconazole, atazanavir and iron salts.
sec.Pregnancy & Lactation: Use only if clearly needed; caution during breast feeding.
sec.Storage: Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light.

nursing: Administer before breakfast; capsule contents may be sprinkled on soft food for patients with swallowing difficulty but pellets must not be crushed.

sec.Indications: Gastric and duodenal ulcer, GERD, reflux oesophagitis, H. pylori eradication, acid aspiration prophylaxis, Zollinger–Ellison syndrome.
sec.Dosage & Administration: Adults: 20 mg once daily for 4–8 weeks; up to 40 mg daily in severe or resistant cases.
sec.Side Effects: Headache, diarrhoea, constipation, abdominal pain, nausea; rarely rash and dizziness.
sec.Contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to omeprazole.
sec.Drug Interactions: Prolongs elimination of diazepam, phenytoin and warfarin; reduces clopidogrel activation.
sec.Pregnancy & Lactation: Can be used in pregnancy where clinically indicated; excreted in breast milk — use with caution.
sec.Storage: Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light.

nursing: For IV use give slowly over 2–5 minutes. Monitor for QT prolongation in patients with cardiac risk factors or on other QT-prolonging drugs; check bowel habits — constipation is common.

sec.Indications: Nausea and vomiting induced by chemotherapy and radiotherapy; prevention and treatment of post-operative nausea and vomiting.
sec.Dosage & Administration: Adults: 8 mg 2–3 times daily orally; for PONV a single 16 mg dose one hour before anaesthesia, or 4–8 mg IV slowly.
sec.Side Effects: Headache, constipation, flushing, sensation of warmth; rarely arrhythmia and hypersensitivity.
sec.Contraindications: Concomitant apomorphine; hypersensitivity to ondansetron.
sec.Drug Interactions: QT-prolonging drugs (amiodarone, some antipsychotics); enzyme inducers such as rifampicin reduce plasma levels.
sec.Pregnancy & Lactation: Avoid in the first trimester unless essential; caution in lactation.
sec.Storage: Store below 30°C, protected from light and moisture.

nursing: Confirm no history of cephalosporin or severe penicillin allergy before the first dose. May be taken with or without food; counsel the patient to complete the full course.

sec.Indications: Upper and lower respiratory tract infections, otitis media, urinary tract infections, typhoid fever, uncomplicated gonorrhoea.
sec.Dosage & Administration: Adults and children over 10 years: 200–400 mg daily in 1–2 divided doses, usually for 7 days. Children: 8 mg/kg/day.
sec.Side Effects: Diarrhoea and stool changes are most frequent; nausea, abdominal pain, headache; rarely hypersensitivity reactions.
sec.Contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to cephalosporin antibiotics.
sec.Drug Interactions: May increase prothrombin time — caution with anticoagulants; carbamazepine levels may rise.
sec.Pregnancy & Lactation: Use only if clearly needed; caution in nursing mothers.
sec.Storage: Store below 30°C, protected from light and moisture.

nursing: Reconstitute 1 g with 10 mL water for injection and give IV over 2–4 minutes, or by infusion. Never mix or co-administer with calcium-containing IV solutions. Observe the injection site for phlebitis.

sec.Indications: Septicaemia, pneumonia, meningitis, complicated UTI, bone and soft-tissue infections, surgical prophylaxis, gonorrhoea.
sec.Dosage & Administration: Adults: 1–2 g once daily IV or IM (up to 4 g in severe infection). Children: 50–80 mg/kg/day.
sec.Side Effects: Pain at injection site, phlebitis, diarrhoea, rash, eosinophilia; rarely biliary pseudolithiasis.
sec.Contraindications: Cephalosporin hypersensitivity; neonates with hyperbilirubinaemia; concurrent IV calcium in neonates.
sec.Drug Interactions: Incompatible with calcium-containing solutions (Ringer’s lactate); aminoglycosides must be given separately.
sec.Pregnancy & Lactation: Use only when clearly indicated; low concentrations excreted in breast milk.
sec.Storage: Store dry powder below 30°C, protected from light. Use reconstituted solution within 6 hours at room temperature.

nursing: Always ask about penicillin allergy before the first dose and observe for rash or anaphylaxis. Encourage completion of the full course even after symptoms resolve.

sec.Indications: ENT infections, lower respiratory tract infections, UTI, skin and soft-tissue infections, dental abscess, H. pylori eradication regimens.
sec.Dosage & Administration: Adults: 250–500 mg every 8 hours. Children: 25–50 mg/kg/day in divided doses.
sec.Side Effects: Nausea, diarrhoea, skin rash; rarely antibiotic-associated colitis and hypersensitivity reactions.
sec.Contraindications: Penicillin hypersensitivity; caution in infectious mononucleosis (high incidence of rash).
sec.Drug Interactions: Allopurinol increases rash risk; may reduce efficacy of oral contraceptives; probenecid raises amoxicillin levels.
sec.Pregnancy & Lactation: Generally regarded as safe when clearly indicated.
sec.Storage: Store below 30°C in a dry place.

nursing: Do not give antacids, iron, zinc or dairy within 2 hours of the dose (chelation reduces absorption). Encourage generous fluid intake; tell the patient to report tendon pain immediately.

sec.Indications: UTI, typhoid fever, GI infections, respiratory tract infections, bone and joint infections, gonorrhoea, septicaemia.
sec.Dosage & Administration: Adults: 250–750 mg twice daily for 5–14 days depending on severity and site of infection.
sec.Side Effects: Nausea, diarrhoea, dizziness, headache; rarely tendinitis/tendon rupture, QT prolongation, photosensitivity.
sec.Contraindications: Quinolone hypersensitivity; generally avoided in children, pregnancy and lactation; history of quinolone-associated tendon disorder.
sec.Drug Interactions: Antacids and mineral supplements impair absorption; raises theophylline levels; potentiates warfarin; caution with QT-prolonging drugs.
sec.Pregnancy & Lactation: Avoid — arthropathy demonstrated in immature animals.
sec.Storage: Store below 30°C, protected from light.

nursing: Give with or after food to reduce GI upset. Strictly no alcohol during therapy and for 48 hours after — disulfiram-like reaction. Warn that urine may darken.

sec.Indications: Amoebiasis, giardiasis, trichomoniasis, anaerobic bacterial infections, antibiotic-associated colitis, H. pylori regimens, surgical prophylaxis.
sec.Dosage & Administration: Adults: 400 mg three times daily for 5–7 days (amoebiasis: 800 mg three times daily for 5 days).
sec.Side Effects: Metallic taste, nausea, GI upset, furred tongue, dark urine; peripheral neuropathy on prolonged use.
sec.Contraindications: Hypersensitivity to nitroimidazoles; first trimester of pregnancy; chronic alcohol dependence.
sec.Drug Interactions: Disulfiram-like reaction with alcohol; potentiates warfarin; lithium levels may rise; phenytoin and phenobarbital reduce its effect.
sec.Pregnancy & Lactation: Avoid in the first trimester; enters breast milk — may give milk a bitter taste.
sec.Storage: Store below 30°C, protected from light.

nursing: Give with water, not fruit juice (reduces absorption). Non-sedating at usual doses, but assess individual response before activities requiring alertness.

sec.Indications: Seasonal allergic rhinitis, chronic idiopathic urticaria.
sec.Dosage & Administration: Adults and children over 12 years: 120 mg once daily for rhinitis; 180 mg once daily for urticaria.
sec.Side Effects: Headache, drowsiness (rare), dizziness, nausea, fatigue.
sec.Contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to fexofenadine.
sec.Drug Interactions: Aluminium/magnesium antacids within 2 hours reduce absorption; erythromycin and ketoconazole raise plasma levels without QT effect.
sec.Pregnancy & Lactation: Use only if clearly needed; caution during breast feeding.
sec.Storage: Store below 30°C, protected from moisture.

nursing: Give in the evening. Not for relief of an acute asthma attack — ensure rescue bronchodilator is available. Report mood or behaviour changes.

sec.Indications: Prophylaxis and chronic treatment of asthma, exercise-induced bronchoconstriction, seasonal allergic rhinitis.
sec.Dosage & Administration: Adults and adolescents 15 years and over: 10 mg once daily in the evening.
sec.Side Effects: Headache, abdominal pain, thirst; rarely sleep disturbance and neuropsychiatric events.
sec.Contraindications: Hypersensitivity to montelukast.
sec.Drug Interactions: Phenobarbital and rifampicin reduce plasma levels; no dose adjustment usually required.
sec.Pregnancy & Lactation: Use only if clearly needed.
sec.Storage: Store below 30°C, protected from light and moisture.

nursing: Record BP before administration. Check for ankle oedema at each shift; advise the patient not to stop the drug abruptly.

sec.Indications: Hypertension, chronic stable angina, vasospastic (Prinzmetal’s) angina.
sec.Dosage & Administration: Adults: initially 5 mg once daily, increased to 10 mg once daily if required.
sec.Side Effects: Ankle oedema, headache, flushing, dizziness, palpitations, fatigue.
sec.Contraindications: Hypersensitivity to dihydropyridines; severe hypotension; cardiogenic shock.
sec.Drug Interactions: CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, ritonavir) raise levels; limit simvastatin to 20 mg daily with amlodipine.
sec.Pregnancy & Lactation: Avoid unless no safer alternative.
sec.Storage: Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light.

nursing: Monitor BP, serum potassium and creatinine. First-dose hypotension possible in volume-depleted patients — give the first dose with the patient seated or in bed.

sec.Indications: Hypertension, diabetic nephropathy in type 2 diabetes, heart failure, stroke risk reduction in LVH.
sec.Dosage & Administration: Adults: usual starting and maintenance dose 50 mg once daily; range 25–100 mg in 1–2 doses.
sec.Side Effects: Dizziness, hyperkalaemia, hypotension, fatigue; cough less common than with ACE inhibitors.
sec.Contraindications: Pregnancy; hypersensitivity; concomitant aliskiren in diabetes.
sec.Drug Interactions: Potassium-sparing diuretics and potassium supplements raise hyperkalaemia risk; NSAIDs blunt effect; lithium levels may rise.
sec.Pregnancy & Lactation: Contraindicated — fetal toxicity; avoid during breast feeding.
sec.Storage: Store below 30°C, protected from light.

nursing: Instruct the patient to report unexplained muscle pain, tenderness or weakness. Periodic LFT monitoring; avoid grapefruit juice in quantity.

sec.Indications: Hypercholesterolaemia, mixed dyslipidaemia, primary and secondary prevention of cardiovascular events.
sec.Dosage & Administration: Adults: 10–20 mg once daily, any time of day; maximum 80 mg daily.
sec.Side Effects: Myalgia, GI upset, headache, raised transaminases; rarely myopathy and rhabdomyolysis.
sec.Contraindications: Active liver disease, unexplained persistent transaminase elevation, pregnancy and lactation.
sec.Drug Interactions: Macrolides, azole antifungals, ciclosporin and grapefruit juice raise myopathy risk; potentiates some anticoagulants.
sec.Pregnancy & Lactation: Contraindicated.
sec.Storage: Store below 30°C, protected from light and moisture.

nursing: Give in the morning to avoid nocturia. Maintain strict intake–output chart and daily weight; monitor electrolytes. IV doses must be given slowly (max 4 mg/min) to avoid ototoxicity.

sec.Indications: Oedema of cardiac, hepatic or renal origin; acute pulmonary oedema; hypertension; oliguria due to renal insufficiency.
sec.Dosage & Administration: Adults: 20–80 mg as a single morning dose; may be titrated. IV 20–50 mg slowly in emergencies.
sec.Side Effects: Hypokalaemia, hyponatraemia, dehydration, hypotension, hyperuricaemia; ototoxicity with rapid IV injection.
sec.Contraindications: Anuria, severe hypokalaemia or hyponatraemia, hepatic coma, sulfonamide hypersensitivity.
sec.Drug Interactions: Increases digoxin toxicity via hypokalaemia; aminoglycosides add ototoxicity; NSAIDs reduce diuretic effect; lithium levels rise.
sec.Pregnancy & Lactation: Only if essential; may suppress lactation.
sec.Storage: Store below 30°C, protected from light.

nursing: Check apical pulse before each dose — withhold and inform the physician if below 60/min. Never stop abruptly; taper over 1–2 weeks. Caution in diabetics: masks hypoglycaemia symptoms.

sec.Indications: Hypertension, angina, cardiac arrhythmias, migraine prophylaxis, essential tremor, anxiety, thyrotoxicosis (adjunct).
sec.Dosage & Administration: Adults: 10–40 mg 2–3 times daily depending on indication; titrate to response.
sec.Side Effects: Bradycardia, fatigue, cold extremities, sleep disturbance, bronchospasm.
sec.Contraindications: Asthma/COPD, uncontrolled heart failure, marked bradycardia, second/third-degree heart block, cardiogenic shock.
sec.Drug Interactions: Verapamil/diltiazem risk severe bradycardia; masks sympathetic response to hypoglycaemia with insulin; NSAIDs reduce antihypertensive effect.
sec.Pregnancy & Lactation: Use only if essential — fetal growth restriction and neonatal bradycardia reported.
sec.Storage: Store below 30°C in a dry place.

nursing: Give with or immediately after meals to limit GI upset. Withhold before and for 48 hours after iodinated contrast studies; monitor renal function and B12 on long-term use.

sec.Indications: First-line therapy of type 2 diabetes mellitus; polycystic ovary syndrome (off-label adjunct).
sec.Dosage & Administration: Adults: initially 500 mg 1–2 times daily with meals, titrated weekly; maximum 2550 mg daily in divided doses.
sec.Side Effects: Anorexia, nausea, diarrhoea, metallic taste, B12 malabsorption; lactic acidosis rare but serious.
sec.Contraindications: eGFR below 30 mL/min, diabetic ketoacidosis, severe hepatic disease, conditions predisposing to tissue hypoxia.
sec.Drug Interactions: Iodinated contrast media (withhold); alcohol potentiates lactic acidosis; cimetidine raises levels.
sec.Pregnancy & Lactation: Insulin preferred in pregnancy; metformin may be continued on specialist advice.
sec.Storage: Store below 30°C, protected from moisture.

nursing: High-alert: dose must be independently double-checked by a second nurse and drawn only in an insulin syringe. Give SC 30 minutes before a meal; rotate sites; check capillary glucose per protocol and keep hypo-kit available.

sec.Indications: Diabetes mellitus requiring insulin; diabetic ketoacidosis (IV infusion); hyperkalaemia (with glucose).
sec.Dosage & Administration: Individualised. Usual SC dose 0.3–1.0 IU/kg/day in divided doses 30 minutes before meals; IV only as an infusion under monitoring.
sec.Side Effects: Hypoglycaemia (most common), lipodystrophy at injection sites, local hypersensitivity, transient refraction changes.
sec.Contraindications: Hypoglycaemia; hypersensitivity to human insulin or excipients.
sec.Drug Interactions: Beta blockers mask hypoglycaemia; corticosteroids, thiazides and sympathomimetics raise insulin requirement; alcohol potentiates hypoglycaemia.
sec.Pregnancy & Lactation: Insulin is the treatment of choice for diabetes in pregnancy; safe in lactation.
sec.Storage: Unopened vials at 2–8°C (never frozen); in-use vial may be kept below 25°C for up to 6 weeks. Do not use if the solution is not clear and colourless.

nursing: Give with food. Monitor blood glucose, BP and for signs of infection; doses must be tapered — never stopped abruptly after prolonged therapy.

sec.Indications: Inflammatory and allergic disorders, cerebral oedema, croup, severe asthma, antiemetic adjunct in chemotherapy, adrenal insufficiency (with mineralocorticoid).
sec.Dosage & Administration: Adults: 0.5–10 mg daily depending on condition, as a single morning dose or divided; use the lowest effective dose for the shortest time.
sec.Side Effects: Hyperglycaemia, fluid retention, hypertension, mood change, insomnia, peptic ulceration, adrenal suppression, osteoporosis with prolonged use.
sec.Contraindications: Systemic fungal infection; live vaccines during immunosuppressive doses; hypersensitivity.
sec.Drug Interactions: NSAIDs increase GI bleeding risk; reduces effect of antidiabetics; enzyme inducers lower steroid levels; potentiates hypokalaemia with diuretics.
sec.Pregnancy & Lactation: Use only when benefit outweighs risk; compatible with breast feeding at low doses.
sec.Storage: Store below 30°C, protected from light and moisture.
